Content:
Suppose that we wish to find an algebraic expression for [MATH: (f \circ g)(x),] where [MATH: f(x) = 2x + 3] and [MATH: g(x) = x - 1.]

Content:
The composite function can be calculated by taking the expression for the inner function [MATH: {\color{blue}g(x)}] and passing it as input to the outer function [MATH: f({\color{blue}x})\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: (f∘g)(x)|= f(g(x)); = 2(g(x)) + 3; = 2(x − 1) + 3; = 2x − 2 + 3; = 2x + 1]

Content:
So, we just take the expression for [MATH: f] and replace every occurrence of [MATH: x] with the expression for [MATH: g(x).]

sections.normalized_html: Find [MATH: (f \circ g)(x)] for [MATH: f(x) = 3x^2 - 2x] and [MATH: g(x) = x + 4.]

sections.normalized_html:
Note that [MATH: (f \circ g)(x)] is equivalent to [MATH: f(g(x)).]

To find [MATH: f(g(x)),] we write down the function [MATH: f] and replace every occurrence of [MATH: x] with [MATH: g(x)\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: f(x)|= 3x^{2} − 2x; f(g(x))|= 3(g(x))^{2} − 2(g(x))]

Then, we substitute [MATH: {\color{blue}g(x)} = {\color{red}x+4}] into the right-hand side of the above and simplify, as follows:

[MATH: f(g(x))|= 3(g(x))^{2} − 2(g(x)); = 3(x + 4)^{2} − 2(x + 4); = 3(x + 4)(x + 4) − 2x − 8; = 3(x^{2} + 4x + 4x + 16) − 2x − 8; = 3(x^{2} + 8x + 16) − 2x − 8; = 3x^{2} + 24x + 48 − 2x − 8; = 3x^{2} + 22x + 40]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose that we wish to find an algebraic expression for [MATH: (f \circ g)(x),] where [MATH: f(x) = 2x + 3] and [MATH: g(x) = x - 1.]

Content:
The composite function can be calculated by taking the expression for the inner function [MATH: {\color{blue}g(x)}] and passing it as input to the outer function [MATH: f({\color{blue}x})\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: (f∘g)(x)|= f(g(x)); = 2(g(x)) + 3; = 2(x − 1) + 3; = 2x − 2 + 3; = 2x + 1]

Content:
So, we just take the expression for [MATH: f] and replace every occurrence of [MATH: x] with the expression for [MATH: g(x).]

---

Item 2 — Example: Finding a Composite Function

Example Prompt:

Explanation:

To find [MATH: f(g(x)),] we write down the function [MATH: f] and replace every occurrence of [MATH: x] with [MATH: g(x)\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: f(x)|= 3x^{2} − 2x; f(g(x))|= 3(g(x))^{2} − 2(g(x))]

Then, we substitute [MATH: {\color{blue}g(x)} = {\color{red}x+4}] into the right-hand side of the above and simplify, as follows:

[MATH: f(g(x))|= 3(g(x))^{2} − 2(g(x)); = 3(x + 4)^{2} − 2(x + 4); = 3(x + 4)(x + 4) − 2x − 8; = 3(x^{2} + 4x + 4x + 16) − 2x − 8; = 3(x^{2} + 8x + 16) − 2x − 8; = 3x^{2} + 24x + 48 − 2x − 8; = 3x^{2} + 22x + 40]
